mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A3 2.0 TDI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost varies based on the engine's condition and specific code (e.g., CUNA vs DFGA). Used engines typically range from £900 to £2,500. Reconditioned units cost between £2,200 and £4,500. Fully rebuilt engines with warranties range from £3,200 to £6,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of EGR or DPF failure in an Audi A3 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Emissions system failures are the most common reason for Audi A3 2.0 TDI engine replacement requests. Persistent engine management light (EML) with DPF/EGR codes. Noticeable loss of power or frequent limp mode activation. Excessive black smoke from the exhaust or a strong sulphur smell.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Audi A3 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's current market value and overall condition. For 2013-2016 models valued around £6,000-£10,000, a £3,000+ rebuilt engine is a sound investment if the rest of the car is well-maintained. For sub-£4,000 examples, a cheaper used engine or evaluating the scrap value may be more financially prudent.

mainEntity.name: How long does an Audi A3 2.0 TDI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service is highly efficient and minimises downtime. The physical removal and installation typically takes 8 to 11 hours of labour. Most UK specialists can complete the entire supply and fit process within 2 to 3 working days. This includes ECU adaptation, fluid top-ups, and comprehensive road testing.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CUNA and DFGA engine codes in the Audi A3 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: They represent different generations of the 2.0L diesel architecture with distinct maintenance profiles. CUNA is an EA189 engine (2013-2020) known for high torque but susceptible to DPF/EGR coking. DFGA is the newer EA288 evo engine (2020-present) featuring twin-dosing AdBlue for stricter emissions. The DFGA is generally more robust but introduces different AdBlue system failure points to monitor.

historyTimeline.h2: Audi A3 2.0 TDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 2.0 TDI badge launched in the A3 range, it established itself as the definitive high-torque, high-efficiency diesel choice, evolving from robust Pumpe Düse (PD) units to the refined common-rail EA189 and later the advanced EA288 engines.

milestones.description: BMN (2.0L TDI PD, 170hp) introduced for high-spec 8P models, offering strong performance but requiring strict maintenance.
Transition to common-rail EA189 2.0 TDI (CFFB/CFHC, 140-150hp) for improved refinement, efficiency, and emissions compliance.
8V generation launch featuring the updated EA189 (CUNA 150hp/184hp, CRLB 184hp) with enhanced turbocharging and efficiency.
8Y generation introduces the EA288 evo 2.0 TDI (DFGA, 150hp), featuring twin-dosing AdBlue technology for strict Euro 6d compliance and improved long-term reliability.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Audi A3 2.0 TDI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Audi A3 2.0 TDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Audi A3 2.0 TDI is generally a robust powerplant, but high-mileage examples, particularly those with the EA189 engine code (CUNA, CFHC), are prone to emissions system degradation. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: EGR Valve & DPF Blockage - Why the Audi A3 2.0 TDI (EA189) Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Frequent short trips prevent the DPF from reaching optimal regeneration temperatures, while the EGR valve accumulates carbon soot, restricting airflow and potentially contaminating the oil system.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical cleaning of EGR and forced DPF regeneration
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix; high recurrence rate if driving habits do not change.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The definitive solution for catastrophic DPF/EGR-induced engine damage or excessive oil consumption.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2013-2016 Audi A3 2.0 TDI (8V) is valued between £6,000 and £12,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. A rebuilt engine at £3,200-£5,000 represents a viable investment if you plan to keep the vehicle for 2+ years. For sub-£5,000 examples, a used engine replacement may be more financially prudent.
problems.recommendation: If the engine block is intact and compression is good, a specialist DPF/EGR clean or component replacement is the most cost-effective first step. However, if the turbocharger has failed and sent debris into the oil system, a full rebuilt engine replacement is the only safe long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt CUNA Audi A3 2.0 TDI engine prices

problems.h4: AdBlue System & EGR Cooler Leaks - EA288 Specific Vulnerabilities
problems.rootCause: Crystallisation of AdBlue fluid can block dosing lines or damage the NOx sensor, while thermal stress can cause the EGR cooler to develop internal coolant leaks into the combustion chamber.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing dosing valve, pump, or NOx sensor
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective for isolated emissions faults without internal engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, updated EA288 evo components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary only if coolant leakage from the EGR cooler has caused hydrolock or severe internal corrosion.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A 2020+ Audi A3 35 TDI (8Y) holds a strong market value of £14,000 to £25,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. At this valuation, a £3,800-£6,000 rebuilt engine replacement is a minor fraction of the car's worth and fully justified to protect your asset.
problems.recommendation: Address AdBlue warnings immediately. Early intervention with a specialist sensor or dosing unit replacement is inexpensive compared to the catastrophic engine failure that can result from ignored coolant leaks into the combustion chamber.
